arguments.value: Stallhub prohibited-items policy (updated 15 Sep 2026), fetched 2026-09-29, attemptId 8db0ca8f-0000-4000-8000-000000000007, URL https://stallhub.example/policies/prohibited: says "Digital templates (spreadsheets, planners, trackers) remain permitted". It prohibits PLR resale without a licence and IP-infringing items, so build original content only. NOT yet checked: Stallhub seller-account identity/KYC rules. Only the owner can open an account; never invent identity facts.

PRODUCT: an original Google Sheets/Excel bookkeeping sheet for UK self-employed dog groomers. Tabs: income by dog and service type; expenses and stock (shampoo, blades); mileage log for mobile groomers; year-end summary for the self-employed tax return. The listing must say plainly it is NOT HMRC-compatible MTD filing software and not tax advice. Differentiator: the mileage tracking the £12 competitor lacks (a review said "doesn't do mileage").
COST: about £1–5 of AI usage to build, plus the 15p listing fee. Total spend about £5.
TIME: about 1 day to build, then 45 days of observation.
PRICE: £12 (nets about £10.54).
OWNER ASKS (nothing is paid until approved): (1) a Stallhub seller account operated by the owner; (2) approval for the 15p listing fee. Use request_spend only with an owner-enrolled dst_ id, citing attempts …0003, …0006 and …0007.
DECISION RULES after 45 days live:
- SUCCESS: ≥5 sales at ≥£12, with ≤1 refund or complaint. Then iterate features and consider £15.
- FAIL: ≤1 sale, OR a sales rate no better than the existing £12 listing (14 sales, time on sale unknown). Then stop and propose a failure lesson to fleet knowledge.
- 2–4 sales: make ONE change (title, preview or price) and decide after another 30 days.
Only real external sales count. Record the date the listing went live when it does.

STATUS at 2026-09-29: research is done. O2 chosen (goal g1 open). Nothing built, no spend requested, no revenue.
UNCERTAINTIES:
- Small market: the best existing listing has only 14 sales.
- Stated vs real demand: forum posters are self-selected; one said they would pay £10–15, but none mentioned actually buying.
- Retention: one poster gave up on a template after a week.
- MTD scope: don't overclaim.
- Search volume is a modelled estimate (±40%).
- Stallhub seller KYC rules are unchecked.
NEXT STEPS: (1) Check Stallhub seller/identity requirements. (2) Ask the owner for the account and listing-fee approval. (3) Build the sheet in the workspace. (4) Track sales from launch.
REFERENCES: attemptIds appear as suffixes …0001 to …0006. Only …0007's full id is confirmed (8db0ca8f-0000-4000-8000-000000000007); the others probably share the prefix, so verify before citing the full id. Saved research pages may have been pruned; rely on these notes.
FLEET KNOWLEDGE: kp-1 (Gigsly bans automated-agent seller accounts and requires personal ID and a bank account in the seller's own name, attempt …0005) is pending the owner's decision. O3 is not viable on Gigsly.

arguments.title: Stallhub allows digital templates but bans PLR resale without a licence
arguments.content: Stallhub's prohibited-items policy (last updated 15 Sep 2026) says: "Digital templates (spreadsheets, planners, trackers) remain permitted." It prohibits weapons, counterfeit goods, adult content, IP-infringing items, and resale of private-label-rights (PLR) content without a licence. For fleet agents: original templates are allowed; resold PLR packs are not unless licensed. Source: https://stallhub.example/policies/prohibited, attemptId 8db0ca8f-0000-4000-8000-000000000007, fetched 2026-09-29. Not yet checked: the identity/KYC rules for opening a seller account. Re-check the policy before relying on it, as it may change.

arguments.value: On 2026-09-29 I proposed "Stallhub allows digital templates but bans PLR resale without a licence" (policy, citing …0007). The system returned id kp-1, pending owner review. Earlier notes say a Gigsly-ban lesson was also kp-1. The ids clash, so check with read_knowledge whether the Gigsly lesson was actually recorded. If it wasn't, re-propose it (Gigsly ToS bans automated-agent/on-behalf accounts and requires personal photo ID and a bank account in the seller's own name, attempt …0005). O1 saturation is only an observation, not a tested failure, so don't propose it as a lesson.
